about: The committed matrix of docs/upstream-parity.md (decision D6): each cell holds an image of wz to the original built by this repository, with the verdict of decision D1 (WIN, TIE or LOSS; only WIN counts). The rows of a run are the output of `scripts/lib/kit_compare.py --format rows` for that run, never figures copied by hand; a change that moves a cell moves its run here, in the same commit, with the run that measured it.

runs.target: mcu-zephyr: the T2G kit (CYT4BF, Cortex-M7 at 350 MHz) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd 1.10.0 with its REST plugin on the bench host
runs.workload: W1: answer the two GETs of the wz client's keys, 2,000 times each per boot, through the router
runs.method: scripts/kit-lane.sh compare --boots 12, compare builds (CONFIG_WZ_MEMORY_REPORT), images alternated per round, turnaround read at the host's wire
runs.reference: zephyr-pico-queryable-st: zenoh-pico with the wz client's planes (queryable, UDP unicast) in its single-threaded arm, the stronger of its two arms in every cell of this run
runs.tree: origin's main at 1d234b06ba, with the SCE pin at 6ba84c3f37 (the engine's Appendix D once for the program, over packed table rows, events as numbers, its constructor and exit walk out of line), the Request's Put and Del arms out of the zenoh-preset images (CONFIG_WZ_REQUEST_PUT_DEL=n), the Arm EABI zeroing and filling calls answered by the libc memset, the receive's reading of a handshake message out of line from the frame that gives the engine the event, the connect manager ordering its rows by swaps, and the send's dispatch as one copy that calls the message's encoder through a pointer; sent to the bench host
caveats: Two programs written for one workload, the same keys, bodies and encoding on the wire (decision D4): the cells move to pico's own programs on both libraries when the pico C ABI runs on the MCU (step M5).

The ram cell holds each image's static RAM, which includes the kernel heap pool each image is configured with (128 KiB for pico and for the wz heap client); the smallest pool each image runs in is not measured yet, so a ram WIN against pico is not yet a claim.

Both sides of this run poll the receive path out of the ITCM (CONFIG_WZ_POLL_PATH_IN_ITCM). The turnaround of the fixed client reads 0.1900 ms against 0.2027 for the single-threaded pico (the pico read 0.1988 in run 20261028T114528): the kit's session moved between runs, and the ratio, 0.9376 (interval 0.9235 to 0.9746, twelve boots of each image), is what holds.

The heap client's turnaround reads TIE here (0.9947) where it read LOSS in run 20261028T114528 (1.0156). Its source changed only by what the fixed client's did; the difference was not examined and is within what the interval of one run allows.

The text cells are of the compare builds, which carry the memory report: the fixed client reads 144,456 bytes here and 143,356 in the build the kit lane's text gate holds (deploy/text_budget.json), 1,100 more. The reference's text fell from 145,364 (run 20261028T114528) to 144,836: 504 of the 528 bytes are the board hooks' answer to the Arm EABI zeroing and filling calls, which both images link and call, so the wz image fell by the same 504 and the ratio did not move; the other 24 bytes were not examined.

The stack_used cell is the difference of two sums of thread readings, and only the difference is the cell's: both images read 368 bytes less than in run 20261028T114528 (the pico 5,692 against 6,060) by the amount the receive thread of the Ethernet driver they share changed in the wz console between two builds (1,948 to 1,580 bytes), the cause of which was not examined. The wz client reads 5,652 against 5,692, 40 bytes (0.7 percent) under; its main thread's reading is 2,720 and is the receive of a handshake message, not a query's answer.

The margins are small: text 380 bytes (0.26 percent), flash 476 (0.33) and stack_used 40 (0.7) under the reference. Text and flash are of deterministic builds, so they hold until a change moves them; a change is read against these margins and not against the verdict.

The text and the instruction-cache layout move together on this kit: the same source read 41.4 and 42.0 us in the stamps with 392 bytes of unreached code between them, so a turnaround difference below a microsecond is not attributed to a source change.
